partner_context: Yango is the Dubai-headquartered global ride-tech platform operating across the Middle East, Africa, the Caspian and South Asia. Critically — and this is the lead frame for every conversation — this is the **Dubai-HQ'd Yango**, headquartered and operationally based in the UAE, with its growth centred on the GCC, Africa and emerging coastal markets. That footprint maps almost perfectly onto the world's most underbuilt waterfronts: lagoon megacities, Gulf jetty networks, Red Sea resorts and Caspian bays where the road is congested and the water is empty.

hero.title: Yango × Navier — the water tier for the Dubai-HQ'd global ride platform
hero.subtitle: From Dubai's jetties to Lagos's lagoon and the Caspian shore — a foiling water tier in the Yango app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Yango-branded electric-foiling water-mobility tier across Yango's strongest markets — anchored in its home UAE, spanning African lagoon megacities (Lagos, Abidjan, Dakar), the GCC (Qatar, Saudi commercial), Türkiye's Bosphorus and Aegean, Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, and the Caspian — booked in the same Yango app, on the same wallet, as the car.

why_now: Yango is scaling aggressively beyond ride-hailing into a multimodal super-app, exactly as Navier's N30 Pioneer II becomes commercially available. Yango's geography is uniquely water-shaped: Dubai (its HQ) has the densest luxury-jetty network on earth; Lagos, Abidjan and Dakar are lagoon-and-island megacities choked by bridges; the Bosphorus is the world's busiest commuter strait; the Red Sea and Caspian are building marine-first tourism. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the dense short-water corridors across all of them, with Quanta-LR staged honestly for the longer regional legs.
network_thesis: Yango's water network shares one global corridor registry with the other partners — the same canonical geometry, country tags and boarding points — but renders as Yango's own branded view with its own economics. Where corridors overlap with another partner (the UAE jetties, Doha Bay, the Jeddah/Red Sea coast), Yango inherits the shared canonical routes rather than recreating them; where Yango is alone (the African lagoons, the Caspian), it extends the shared registry. This is hub-and-spoke at platform scale: one home-market flagship (UAE) proving the model, then a deliberate spoke-by-spoke rollout across Africa, the GCC, Türkiye, Egypt and the Caspian.
multimodal_fit: Same Yango app, same wallet, same account: a Yango car to the jetty, a foiling hop across the bay or lagoon, a Yango ride on arrival. In Yango's home UAE and across its African strongholds, the multimodal water leg is frequently the fastest part of the journey — and it never leaves the Yango ecosystem.
differentiation: Against Yango's incumbent competitors, a foiling water tier is a category nobody else offers — a defensible, premium, all-electric mode on exactly the congested-bridge and slow-ferry corridors where Yango's markets hurt most. Against the diesel ferries and water taxis it replaces: faster, quiet, low-wake, zero-local-emission and on-demand. Against road: a direct line that skips the gridlock.

proof_points.claim: Yango is Dubai-HQ'd with its strongest base in the UAE.
proof_points.evidence: The UAE is both Yango's headquarters and the world's densest premium water-mobility market — the natural home-market flagship.

proof_points.claim: Yango's African footprint is lagoon-and-island shaped.
proof_points.evidence: Lagos (lagoon), Abidjan (Ébrié Lagoon, proven bateaux-bus demand), Dakar (Gorée/island runs) and Maputo Bay are all water-natural megacities where Yango already operates ridehail.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are real, range-gated and shared.
proof_points.evidence: 183 modeled corridors across 15 countries, sharing canonical geometry with the broader partner network and inheriting correct country tags.

proof_points.claim: Vessel sizing is honest by leg.
proof_points.evidence: Every corridor is range-gated — ≤70nm on commercial-now Pioneer II, 75–150nm on roadmap Quanta-LR, longer legs rendered aspirational — never a long leg faked on a short-range boat.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Prove (UAE home-market flagship + first African lagoon)
phases.narrative: Launch the dense intra-Dubai jetty network in Yango's home market on Pioneer II, alongside a first proven African lagoon anchor (Lagos or Abidjan). Prove unit economics where willingness-to-pay is highest and demand is densest.
phases.rationale: Anchor on the home-market flagship and a proven lagoon-commute base before spreading; highest-density, lowest-friction water.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Scale (Africa + GCC + Türkiye + Egypt, N30 + N35)
phases.narrative: Replicate the proven playbook across the African lagoon megacities (Lagos, Abidjan, Dakar, Maputo), the GCC (Doha Bay, Jeddah/Red Sea commercial), the Istanbul Bosphorus and İzmir/Aegean, and Egypt's Red Sea and Nile — adding the N35 Shuttle on the densest corridors to roughly double throughput per hull.
phases.rationale: Spoke-by-spoke rollout across Yango's strongest markets once the flagship proves the model; N35 lifts peak-corridor economics.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Mature & extend (Quanta-LR regional reach + Caspian + in-app default)
phases.narrative: Open the Quanta-LR regional and trans-water legs (Dubai–Abu Dhabi already in Pioneer range, the giga-project coast, the Caspian and Aegean crossings staged honestly), reach the Caspian markets (Baku, Aktau), and mature into induced demand and full in-app default-operator capture across the network.
phases.rationale: Honest long-range staging plus default-operator monetization once the dense network is proven; held/sovereign markets (Israel) remain data-only until coordination clears.

the_ask: Co-launch a Yango-branded foiling water tier — anchor in Yango's home UAE with a 3-boat Pioneer II flagship across Dubai's jetties, prove a first African lagoon market in parallel, then roll out spoke-by-spoke across Africa, the GCC, Türkiye, Egypt and the Caspian on the shared corridor network.
close: Yango's Dubai-HQ'd, Africa-and-GCC-heavy footprint is the best-shaped ride-platform geography in the world for water mobility: its busiest markets are lagoon megacities, Gulf jetty networks and congested straits where a foiling tier is both a category nobody else has and the fastest leg of the journey. The home market proves it; the network scales it.
end_state: A Yango water tier spanning its home UAE flagship, the African lagoon megacities, the GCC, the Türkiye straits and Aegean, Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, and the Caspian — one shared corridor network, rendered as Yango's branded view, booked in the Yango app.
